articles.excerpt: Short answer: For a gaming supplier-invoice workflow, the best LLM API for an in-app chatbot in Node.js is a currently available chat model such as deepseek-v4.1-flash behind /v1/chat/completions, wit…
articles.body: Short answer: For a gaming supplier-invoice workflow, the best LLM API for an in-app chatbot in Node.js is a currently available chat model such as deepseek-v4.1-flash behind /v1/chat/completions , with schema-shaped JSON and a small provider adapter. The important choice is the output contract, not the brand on the model. The hard part is not getting text on the screen. It is keeping invoice_number , currency , line_items , and total stable when the model or backend changes. A conversational answer can be approximate. An accounting record cannot. I would make the first implementation boring enough to test: stream the operator-facing reply, collect the extraction result, validate it in application code, and send anything ambiguous to review.

articles.title: For one month, EIA's U.S. power plant inventory listed 28 reactors retired before 2002
articles.excerpt: EIA's monthly generator inventory, EIA-860M, has a Retired sheet. EIA's page gives its scope as generators retired since 2002. Before EIA published its September 2026 file, I fixed a bar: fewer than 1…
articles.body: EIA's monthly generator inventory, EIA-860M, has a Retired sheet. EIA's page gives its scope as generators retired since 2002. Before EIA published its September 2026 file, I fixed a bar: fewer than 10 generators would leave that sheet. 16 left, so the bar failed. Then I checked who they were. All 16 are nuclear units retired between 1972 and 1998, from Maine Yankee to Zion, 8,663.1 MW in all. By my rebuilt changelog, none of them was listed in any monthly file from July 2015 to July 2026. They first appear in August 2026 and are gone in September. August had 28 such rows, not 16. Another 12 reactors retired before 2002 have no plant ID, so a reader that needs one never sees them. Among them are Shippingport, Indian Point 1, Shoreham and Fort St. Vrain.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.

articles.body: NASA/Danny Nowlin Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with a 111% power level. For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket. Prior to use, all RS-25 engines are proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis. While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime engine contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability.

articles.body: Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.
